column1: # p290 — 2026-10-18 — ACTION p290: THE SUBMODULE BOUNDARY AS A GRANT AXIS.
# The question: when a repository's MIT payload sits in a superproject whose content is seven
# `160000 commit` gitlinks, WHAT DOES THE GRANT COVER?
# 🔵 Why this is not an axis this base already had.  Every prior instrument asks WHERE the
# grant is (`p215` path, `p969` root-only, `p742` body-vs-reference, `p259` location class) or
# WHAT IT SAYS (`p287` family, `p289` authority-vs-restatement).  A gitlink asks neither: the
# payload is present, at the root, authoritative, and verbatim — and the bytes a studio would
# actually vendor are NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY AT ALL.
# 🔴 The adjacent known shape, for contrast: `p289` found a CATALOGUE licence mistaken for a
# project licence (`ashishpatel26/500-AI-Agents-Projects` — an MIT badge over links it does not
# own).  A gitlink is the same question with a different answer available: a catalogue's targets
# cannot be checked in bulk, a submodule's CAN, because the superproject PINS AN EXACT COMMIT.
# 🟢 THE RULE THIS PASS WRITES DOWN: a submodule grant is verified when (1) the submodule's own
# payload is read first-hand, AND (2) the HEAD that payload was read at EQUALS the gitlink SHA
# the superproject pins.  Condition (2) is what stops this being `ACTION VM` inheritance: the
# commit whose grant was read is the commit a recursive clone lands on.
# 🔴 Where (2) fails — submodule HEAD has moved past the pin — the pin is an UNREAD commit and
# the correct verdict is UNVERIFIED-AT-PIN, not GRANTED.
